question: A customer deploys a media server to distribute streaming videos to network clients. The requirement is to allow the video feed to reach only requesting clients. The shared trees must not propagate the video feed if no clients from that tree request it. To reduce configuration touchpoints, the solution must support the automatic discovery and announcement of RP-set information. Each router in the network is responsible for selecting the RP. Which configuration set meets these requirements?
options:
router(config-if)# ip pim bidir-enable
router(config)# ip pim ssm default
router(config)# ip igmp version 3

router(config-if)# ip pim dense-mode
router(config)# ip pim rp-address 1.1.1.1
router(config)# ip pim rp listener

router(config-if)# ip pim sparse-sense mode
router(config)# ip pim auto-rp
router(config)# ip pim send-rp-announce

router(config-if)# ip pim sparse mode
router(config)# ip pim bsr-candidate Lo0
router(config)# ip pim rp-candidate Lo0
theory: PIM sparse mode builds shared and source trees only in response to explicit receiver joins, so a video feed is never flooded to parts of the network with no interested clients, satisfying the requirement that shared trees not propagate traffic if no clients request it — unlike dense mode, which floods by default. For the rendezvous point itself to be discovered and elected automatically rather than statically configured on every router, Cisco's Bootstrap Router mechanism is used: routers configured as bsr-candidate advertise themselves to become the bootstrap router that distributes RP-set information fabric-wide, while routers configured as rp-candidate advertise themselves as eligible RPs, letting every router independently learn and agree on the active RP without manual rp-address configuration on each device. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — PIM Sparse Mode and BSR-Based RP Discovery)
